_readme: The one hand-authored artefact. msat_script.json says what the document says;
this says what each turn is FOR — the slot it fills, the value that slot holds,
whether it gates a complete survey, and the condition under which the question
scripts/compile_script.py joins the two into data/msat_spec.json and fails if
they have drifted: a transcribed turn with no entry here, an entry naming a node
the transcription no longer has, a choice slot whose option labels are not the
labels printed in the document, or a condition on a slot that no earlier turn
No Python module names a slot, an option value or a payload key. That is

_note_no_escalation: A survey question a member will not answer is recorded as declined and the
call moves on. There is no escalation path for it: handing a satisfaction
call to a human because someone would rather not rate the staff would be
worse for the member than the missing answer is for us.
Three things DO reach a human, and none of them is a missing answer:
the reschedule the document itself asks for, a member who asks to speak to
a person, and anything that sounds like the member is at risk. The last of
those outranks every other rule in the call.

_note: Lines the agent may speak that the document does not contain. Every one is
a situation the script does not cover but a live call reaches. They are
listed here — rather than written into Python — so the business can review
and approve the exact wording, and so an auditor can see at a glance
everything the agent says that is not in the PDF.
tests/test_script_sources.py fails if a spoken line is neither transcribed
from the document nor declared here.
A plain string is spoken EXACTLY as written. An object with a 'goal' is
spoken in the agent's own words, with the line as the intent — use that
only where fixed phrasing would sound mechanical, never for wording that
has been approved for what it says.
off_script.policyholder_unavailable: Thank you — I'll try again another time. Have a good day.
off_script.wrong_number: I'm sorry to have troubled you. Have a good day.
off_script.do_not_call: Understood — I'll make sure you're not called about this again. Thank you for your time.
off_script.side_request_ack: I'll note that and pass it on to the program team.
off_script.unable_to_continue: Thank you for the time you've given me. I'll close the survey here.

_note: Said whenever the member needs a moment. Generated rather than fixed:
hearing the identical sentence every time they pause is the clearest
possible signal that nobody is really listening.
hold_ack.goal: Tell them warmly that there is no rush and you will wait. One short sentence. Do not repeat the question yet, and do not add anything else.

_note: The member asked for a person. Said exactly: what happens next should
not be paraphrased.
representative_handoff.line: Of course — let me put you through to someone who can help. Please stay on the line.

_note: Said when the member says anything suggesting they are at risk — harm to
themselves, harm or neglect by someone else, or a medical emergency.
Said exactly, and the survey stops there. The agent does not advise, does
not reassure, and does not ask the remaining questions. Whether this line
should also give a crisis number is a decision for the business, and a
regional one — this project will not invent a number.
Wording deliberately promises only what an automated caller can deliver:
getting a person on the line, now.
safeguarding_handoff.line: Thank you for telling me. I'm going to stay with you and bring someone from the team onto the call who can help — please hold the line.

off_script.reschedule_datetime_ask: What date and time would work best for us to call you back?

reschedule_datetime_confirm.line: Perfect — we will call you back at the requested time. Thank you for your time, and have a wonderful day.
reschedule_datetime_confirm.goal: Confirm the reschedule time the member just provided, thank them warmly, and end the call. Keep it brief — one or two short sentences.

policyholder_name.description: the policyholder we were asked to survey, as the work item supplies it

risk_tier.description: the policyholder's risk tier, which decides whether question 5 is asked

reached_policyholder.description: whether the person on the line is the policyholder we asked for

participation_consent.description: whether they have a couple of minutes to answer the questions now

wants_reschedule.description: whether they want the call rescheduled for a better time

reviewed_resources.description: whether they reviewed any program resources — action plans, articles, videos or websites

resource_helpfulness.description: how helpful the resources were in making at least one lifestyle change. Only asked of members who did review them

no_review_reason.description: why they did not review the resources. Only asked of members who did not review them

options.label: No time to review the resources
Not interested in the available resources
Program website (Smart Step portal) was not working

improvement_feedback.description: changes or additions they would like to see. 'No' or 'none' is a complete answer here, not a refusal

liked_most.description: what they liked most about the program. 'No' or 'none' is a complete answer here, not a refusal

would_recommend.description: whether they would recommend the program to people they know

staff_helpful.description: whether program staff were helpful and knowledgeable in guiding them through their action plan

overall_experience.description: their rating of the program overall

vm.01.goal: Leave the program's voicemail message and end the call.

in.01.goal: Introduce yourself as Ida from the Smart Step program and ask to speak to the policyholder by name.

in.02.goal: Thank them for taking the call, say why you are calling, and ask whether they have a couple of minutes for a few questions.

in.03.goal: Offer to reschedule the call for a better time.

in.04.goal: Tell them you are putting them through to someone who can reschedule.

in.05.goal: Thank them for their time and end the call.

sv.00.goal: Say the survey is starting and what it is about.

sv.01.goal: Find out whether they reviewed any of the program resources.

sv.01a.goal: Find out how helpful the resources were in making at least one lifestyle change, and read out the four ratings.

sv.01b.goal: Find out WHY they did not review the resources, and read out the four reasons. Do not ask how helpful the resources were — they have just said they did not see them.

sv.02.goal: Ask what changes or additions would improve the program, and say that no or none is a fine answer.

sv.03.goal: Ask what they liked most about the program, and say that no or none is a fine answer.

sv.04.goal: Ask whether they would recommend the program to people they know.

sv.05.goal: Ask whether program staff were helpful and knowledgeable in guiding them through their action plan.

sv.06.goal: Ask them to rate their experience with the program overall, and read out the four ratings.

cl.01.goal: Say the survey is over, thank them for their time and feedback, and say goodbye.
